content.text:
The lighthouse keeper, Elsie, climbed the 147 iron steps every evening, one hand on the cold rail. Her husband had drowned in a storm years before, and she had kept the light burning ever since, certain that someone out there still needed it.

One night, fog swallowed the coast so completely that she couldn't see her own hand. She turned the lamp, sent its beam sweeping, and waited.

Near dawn, a small fishing boat crept out of the gray, guided home by the steady pulse of light. Its skipper waved from the deck. Elsie raised her hand in reply, and for the first time in years, the ache in her chest eased a little.
